citations.assessment: Acha bar Chanina brings a baraita from the south about trumpet blasts accompanying additional offerings.
Acha bar Chanina brings a different baraita from the south.
Rav Nachman cites Acha’s transmission of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi’s account of the southern elders’ ruling.
An additional report from Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi, about Shema, belongs to a separate notice. The following unit attaches it to another baraita.
The case in Caesarea has the stated Abbahu then Assi chain.
The matching digital text explicitly transmits through Assi and Yochanan, without Ammi. Keep Heilprin’s longer attribution as reported.
Acha bar Chanina transmits in Assi’s name in Yochanan’s name, on fixing the quantity at the time of the vow.
A second Assi–Yochanan report concerns the new-moon blessing. It also names Yaakov bar Idi, who reports a different authority in the same discussion.
The digital chain explicitly has Abaye, Assi and Yochanan. Heilprin’s proposed Ammi is retained as a conjecture.
Acha reports Assi’s account of a direction by Resh Lakish at Sidon.
Acha bar Chanina goes out in patched shoes. A distinct Acha, son of Rav Nachman, supplies the qualification about patches.
The accessible text gives the reported Acha–Achai form inside editorial brackets and another version with Akiva. It does not establish what the siglum designates.
Rabbi Acha permits, transmitting in Rabbi Achai bar Chanina’s name, alternatively Rabbi Yaakov bar Rabbi Chanina. Heilprin’s description compresses the first chain.
The primary text indeed has Rav Adda son of Rabbi Chanina. Heilprin’s emendation remains tentative.
Rav Nachman explains his use of the rule cited in the preceding segment. Rabbi Tavla is an interlocutor rather than the source of Nachman’s citation.
Rabbi Levi speaks in Rabbi Acha bar Chanina’s name in the discussion of the order of the blessings within the cited unit.
